author: Australian Associated Press
description:
• Smith’s Sheffield Shield knock cut short by Michael Neser

  • Opener Konstas pushes claims for Test recall with 42 from 86 balls

Steve Smith has fallen cheaply in his batting comeback, making a laborious 12 for NSW against Queensland in their Sheffield Shield clash.

Smith hadn’t played a innings since 22 October, when he battled a neck injury in Australia’s second Test in South Africa. The star batsman returned for NSW ahead of Australia’s first Test against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth.

Continue reading...
title: Steve Smith toils before falling cheaply on return as Sam Konstas pushes Test claim

author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
description:
Famed for its nearby glacier, Franz Josef village faces ‘catastrophic’ flooding and deaths if action not taken to manage the Waiho River

The small village of Franz Josef sits on the rugged west coast of New Zealand’s South Island, its natural beauty providing the drawcard for a million tourists to pack its hotels, spas and restaurants every year.

But that drawcard – which has turned it into a hotspot for everything from hiking to kayaking and made it one of the country’s most popular destinations – may change the course of the village’s fate once again.

Continue reading...
title: Natural beauty made this New Zealand tourist village. Now it threatens its existence

author: Yvonne C Lam
description:
For ABC documentary The Great Food Con, the host crams in extra chips, crackers and ham – just don’t compare his experiment to Super Size Me

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

There is a segment of The Great Food Con, the ABC’s three-part documentary series on ultra-processed foods, where the host, Craig Reucassel, bites into a chocolate bar and looks deeply unhappy. Any other day, the self-identifying chocoholic would be “thrilled” with his treat; but partway through a five-day experiment of consuming an extra 1,500 calories of ultra-processed foods a day, it feels like a chocolate chomping chore.

Also on his menu? Chips, crackers and ham on top of his regular meals. After lunch, he shovels some instant noodles; after breakfast, he bites into a brownie. He is not having a
title: Craig Reucassel on his five-day ‘nightmare’ ultra-processed food diet

author: Exclusive by Matt Hughes
description:
• Fox has broadcasted men’s World Cups in US since 2018

  • Netflix will carry the 2027 Women’s World Cup

  • Netflix tabled largest offer in first round: sources

Fifa’s auction for 2030 World Cup TV rights in the United States has gone to a second round, with the world governing body aiming to create a bidding war between Netflix and Fox Sports/Univision.

Sources with knowledge of the process have told the Guardian that Netflix submitted the largest bid before last week’s deadline and are now regarded as frontrunners, with Fifa understood to have invited second bids in an attempt to drive up the price.

Continue reading...
title: Fifa open second round of 2030 World Cup US media bids with Fox and Netflix

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
High costs during Chad Bianco’s failed run for governor, including a $665 steak dinner, have raised concerns

A southern California county spent more than $3m in a year on a security detail for its sheriff, Chad Bianco, a former Republican candidate for governor, and taxpayers footed the bill for items such as hotels rooms, travel and a $665 steak dinner.

A report from the Riverside county auditor-controller showed costs surged during the final months of Bianco’s gubernatorial campaign, peaking at $439,000 in April, and included flights, hotels, rental cars and meals for security personnel for campaign events.

Continue reading...
title: Republican sheriff racked up $3m security bill for California taxpayers, including Ritz-Carlton stays and steak

author: Presented by Madeleine Finlay with Fiona Harvey , produced by Madeleine Finlay and Joshan Chana . The executive producer was Ellie Bury
description:
The longest ever Cop climate talks have ended in failure after countries were unable to agree a deal. The key sticking point was the omission of any mention of fossil fuels in the final draft. To find out how it all went so wrong and what could come next, Madeleine Finlay speaks to Guardian environment editor Fiona Harvey who has been in Antalya, Turkey covering the talks.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31 failed. What happens now? - video

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
PM says closer ties with EU will lower cost of living, with ‘brainstorming’ sessions being mooted to discuss shape of future relationship

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has criticised former prime ministers for being “stuck in the past” amid warnings over re-opening the Brexit debate, with informal talks now set to take place with Brussels about how the UK could forge even closer ties with the EU.

After a major summit between UK and EU leaders on Friday when trade and youth mobility deals were struck, Brussels signalled a willingness to begin “brainstorming” sessions with UK officials and ministers about the shape of the futu
title: Burnham: I won’t listen to ex-Tory PMs who left UK with ‘bad Brexit deal’

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• No 1 to miss Dortmund game but could return for City clash

  • ‘We were worried … he’s better than expected,’ says manager

Mikel Arteta is hopeful the shoulder injury David Raya sustained at Newcastle is not too serious but confirmed the goalkeeper would miss Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.

Raya was forced off in the second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a suspected dislocated shoulder, raising fears he could be sidelined for an extended period. He had an MRI scan on Arsenal’s return to London and was absent from training on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: David Raya’s shoulder injury ‘not too serious’ and no surgery needed for Arsenal goalkeeper

author: Peter Beaumont senior international correspondent
description:
Move would be breach of Outer Space treaty and Partial Nuclear Test Ban treaty, which prohibit placing of nuclear weapons in orbit

The German government has said it is taking very seriously reports that Russia may be planning to launch a satellite armed with a ⁠nuclear weapon ⁠into ​space later this year.

The move – if confirmed – would be a breach of 1967 Outer Space treaty of which Moscow is a signatory as well the 1963 Partial Nuclear Test Ban treaty – which prohibit the placing of nuclear weapons in Earth’s orbit and test detonations in space.

Continue reading...
title: Germany taking seriously reports Russia may be planning to launch nuclear weapons into space

author: Andrew Herrick
description:
I was 22 and didn’t have a heavy vehicle licence. But I was game, in that ‘I’ll-do-anything-once’ kind of way

I only got the job because my boss was desperate. It was peak sales season, November 1978. Our factory in bayside Melbourne had run radio ads featuring an actor pretending to be a burglar boasting how easy it was to rob places that didn’t have our security doors. People wanted their houses fortified for the holidays. Stock requests were flooding in from stores around the city.

Our truckie – let’s call him Kelvin – a corpulent alcoholic with a Chopper moustache, had just been jailed for evading road tax. The firm’s accountant, who’d agreed to fill in, wasn’t fit to drive. He coached the local men’s football team and his wife had just run off with its champion goal-kicker.

Contin
title: A job that changed me: My last shift as a truck driver was nearly done. Then a man shouted ‘You’re on fire!’

author: Ryan Fonseca in Los Angeles
description:
The SkyLink people mover is less than 2.5 miles long but it’s $1bn over budget and has been delayed by four years

What purportedly modern, world-class city has an airport where millions of visitors step off their planes, glide their bags on to the sidewalk and are greeted by a terrifying scrum of bumper-to-bumper traffic?

Welcome to Los Angeles.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s an embarrassment’: how LA’s desperately needed airport tram went off the rails

author: Ima Caldwell in Bundaberg, photography by Blake Sharp-Wiggins and design by Jolie Zhang
description:
The descendants of the thousands ‘blackbirded’ to work and die on Queensland farms and plantations say the truth about the country’s practice of slavery must be told

• Warning: This article contains descriptions of historical events that will be distressing to some readers, and images of South Sea Islanders who have died

  • The Cotton Capital project: how slavery changed the Guardian, Britain and the world

Uncle Graham Tanner’s great-grandfather was enslaved.

Harry Tanner was born in 1855 on Tanna Island in Vanuatu and abducted to work in Queensland’s sugar plantations under a practice known as blackbirding.

Continue reading...
title: ‘They will never be forgotten again’: uncovering the buried history of Australia’s enslaved South Sea Islanders

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
‘I beat the commies with Solidarity,’ former Polish leader tells US audience, but credit was also due elsewhere

More than four decades have passed since Lech Walesa was awarded the Nobel peace prize for leading Poland’s Solidarity trade union’s campaign for workers rights in the teeth of harsh repression from the country’s communist rulers.

But Walesa – Poland’s first democratically elected post-communist president – had very definite thoughts on which US president might have been justly given the prize.

Continue reading...
title: Lech Walesa calls for Nobel peace prize for US president – no, not that one

author: Sam Jones in Rioja, Almería
description:
Party that won just 0.2% of the vote in 2016 is on course for almost 20% this time and could be part of next government

Almost exactly eight years ago, a video clip of a stocky, bearded man riding a horse through western Andalucía went viral in Spain. The rider was Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, the soundtrack was a bombastic snatch of the Lord of the Rings score, and the caption was an equally unsubtle callback to the 700-year fight to wrest the Iberian peninsula from Islamic rule. “La Reconquista comenzará en tierras andaluzas,” it read – the reconquest will begin on Andalucían soil.

Celebrated by some, jeered by others – and inventively lampooned by those with sufficient skill and time on their hands – the video didn’t
title: From mocked to mainstream: how Spain’s far-right Vox transformed its fortunes

author: Press Association
description:
Incident occurred near the end of Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver, with one person taken to hospital

Police have evacuated Manchester’s Co-op Live arena after a substance believed to be teargas was let off in the crowd during a Don Toliver concert.

Greater Manchester police said the incident occurred near the end of the US rapper’s show on Sunday evening.

Continue reading...
title: Manchester’s Co-op Live arena evacuated after apparent tear gas incident at Don Toliver concert

author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with David Byrne; produced by Ivor Manley and May Robson; executive producer Eli Block
description:
The Talking Heads frontman on why breakthroughs in science and the arts are sometimes ignored, and what happens when they are rediscovered

David Byrne has had more than a lifetime’s worth of genius ideas. The kind that influence art and music decades after they first came about. As the frontman of Talking Heads and then as a solo artist, Byrne has made some of the greatest albums of all time.

He tells Nosheen Iqbal about his new book Sleeping Beauties, in which he explores why so many breakthroughs in science, economics and culture were lost on their initial audience and only later revived and acknowledged to be great.

Continue reading...
title: David Byrne on the great ideas that got away – podcast
